exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery or caesarean section)
cohort: The study included all ewes (n=429) and lambs (n=700) presented to a single UK veterinary practice during the 2013-2014 lambing season.
finding: The study found varying immediate and 7-day survival rates for ewes and lambs depending on the mode of delivery, suggesting that survival chances in first opinion practice are comparable or improved relative to hospitalised populations.
mod_finding: Lambs delivered via caesarean section showed higher immediate (77.7% vs 56.9%) and 7-day (62.6% vs 44.7%) survival rates compared to those born via vaginal delivery, while ewe survival was high for both modes of delivery.
